name: Oxygen & altitude

overlay.caption: less oxygen per breath → breathe and pump faster → make more red cells over days

does: Shows there is less oxygen in each breath higher up
Shows breathing and heart rate rising at first to make up for it
Shows the slower fix: more red blood cells over several days, which lets breathing settle
doesnt: Measure any real person — the numbers are illustrative teaching values
Model altitude sickness or anything dangerous; it stays at ski-resort heights
Account for fitness, age or exercise
limits.text: This is a simplified learning model. Real people vary with age, fitness and health. The numbers are illustrative, not measurements of any real person.
limits.wellbeing: A headache or feeling sick on a mountain trip is a reason to rest, drink water and tell an adult.

sources: CK-12 Life Science: respiratory and circulatory systems
NASA / NOAA: how air pressure changes with altitude (student pages)
